Harvey introductory vortex, added 2026-11-06

Implementation: dist/vortex.js, original project code.
No original Balatro game shader, third-party shader source, or library is bundled.

Visual/technical references consulted:
- Azkun/balatroShader author README:
  https://github.com/Azkun/balatroShader
  Describes centered trigonometric rotation, iterative transformations, palette,
  speed and spin controls in a public browser reconstruction.
- React Bits Balatro component overview:
  https://reactbits.dev/backgrounds/balatro
  Demonstrates the swirling paint and crisp pixel treatment.

This project uses independently written polar coordinates, three bounded
sinusoidal domain-warp passes, green/yellow palette bands and subtle pixel grain.
The parent gesture controller supplies a slowly integrated autonomous angle,
signed velocity and drawing energy. The hand builds energy and progress rather
than directly steering the angle. Six recent normalized gesture samples carry
signed pointer displacement, independent of the circular-unlock scoring.
The latest contact reacts immediately, with lighter fading history. A bounded
Gaussian transport and curl field pulls paint in the hand's actual direction,
including reversals and movement through the center, without rotating the page.
The supplied angle drives rotation; velocity changes a small radial twist.
A stronger slow spatial drift and breathing warp
keep the painted ribbons visibly alive between gestures. Movement energy
adds finer nested filaments and warm luminous highlights, plus a brighter
yellow/green palette. Highlight intensity is smoothly bounded, with no flashes.
No time-times-current-velocity expression is used, so speed changes do not jump
the rotation phase. All periodic shader time phases wrap by complete periods.
Reduced motion holds the texture still and removes energy-driven modulation.
Canvas2D fallback blends two precomputed low/high-density paint textures using
movement energy, rotates with the same angle, and applies bounded slow drift
and breathing transforms, with softly masked displaced paint patches at recent
gesture positions. The fallback moves existing paint instead of drawing rings.
It reproduces the energy/brightness transition but
not the full dynamic GLSL deformation; no full-resolution pixels are computed
per animation frame. Rendering is capped at DPR 1.5 and 1.5M pixels.

Balatro and its branding belong to their respective owners; this is an original
green/yellow website treatment inspired by its background, not official assets.
